_comment: DBX campaign script 1, version 2 (CR-LENSMITH-A011-1 report) as a continuous-narration step list. Timings are synthetic at about 385 ms per word, in the engine's timings.json shape (lines.s<index>: durationMs + marks); the end card is the engine's bookend, outside the drive.

steps.label: Hook card
steps.say: How big does a database client need to be?

steps.label: Connections page
steps.say: DBX says: about twenty-five megabytes. One tool for more than a hundred databases. Here it is, with Postgres, Redis and MongoDB already connected.

steps.label: Open Postgres
steps.say: Open [[pg]] Postgres. The sidebar lists every schema and table.

steps.text: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 50
steps.label: Type the query
steps.say: Type a query. Autocomplete already knows the [[columns]] columns.

steps.label: Run with Cmd+Enter
steps.say: [[run]] Run it with Command Enter. The grid fills, sortable and editable in place.

steps.label: Open Redis
steps.say: Now [[redis]] Redis. Same window, same sidebar, no second app.

steps.label: Right-click demo_shop
steps.say: One more thing. [[right]] Right-click the database.

steps.label: Payoff on the ER diagram
steps.say: Every table, every relationship, drawn in one click. Twenty-five megabytes, no Java, no bundled browser. That is DBX.
